How to Fix Incorrect Information About Your Brand in ChatGPT and AI Search

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

To fix incorrect AI search results about your company, you have to correct the sources that ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews rely on, not argue with the chatbot. Most errors trace back to an outdated web page, a directory listing, an old news article or an inconsistent company profile; once those are fixed and re-crawled, the answers usually follow. Feedback buttons and formal requests help at the margins, and regular monitoring tells you whether the correction has worked.

Why AI assistants get facts about your company wrong

AI assistants produce wrong information about a business because they blend two kinds of knowledge: what the model absorbed during training and what it retrieves from the web at the moment of the question. Both can be outdated or contradictory, and the model fills gaps with plausible-sounding guesses.

Typical errors we see for Italian companies include an old registered address in Milan after a move to Bergamo, a former CEO still named as the leader, a product line discontinued years ago, a closed lawsuit described as ongoing, or confusion with a company that has a similar name in another region. Errors from training data persist until the next model update, while errors from live retrieval can be fixed within days or weeks because they depend on pages that are crawled continuously. For context on how these systems are reshaping search, read our piece on AI Overviews and generative search in reputation management.

Finding the sources the models rely on

Start by asking each assistant the questions your customers would ask and note which sources it cites. Perplexity, ChatGPT with search, Copilot and AI Overviews display links next to their answers, and those links are your first list of pages to inspect.

When no source is shown, the error usually comes from a widely repeated statement. Search Google and Bing for the incorrect phrase in quotation marks, in Italian and English, and you will often find the page where it originated: an aggregator that scraped an old press release, a directory profile, a Wikipedia paragraph or a forum thread. Keep a simple table with the wrong statement, the correct fact, the source URL, who controls that page and the date you checked.

Sources that carry the most weight

  • Your own website, especially the About, Contacts and leadership pages.
  • Google Business Profile and Bing Places listings, which feed local answers.
  • Wikipedia and Wikidata entries, where they exist.
  • Official business registers, such as the data in the Registro delle Imprese and directories that copy it.
  • Major Italian and international news coverage.
  • Review platforms, LinkedIn company pages and frequently cited forums.

How to correct AI generated information at the source

Correct AI generated information by updating the pages you control first, then asking third parties to fix theirs, and finally making sure search engines re-crawl everything. The sequence matters because retrieval systems prefer consistent signals from several sources over a single correction.

On your own website, state the key facts plainly in text, not only in images: legal name, VAT number, headquarters, year of foundation, current management and main activities. Add structured data (schema.org Organization with sameAs links to official profiles) so that the same facts are machine-readable. Then request re-indexing in Google Search Console and submit the URLs through Bing Webmaster Tools or IndexNow, since several assistants depend on the Bing index for live answers.

For third-party pages, contact the editor or site owner with a short, documented request: what is wrong, what is correct and a link to proof, such as a chamber of commerce extract. Directories usually update within days. News publishers are more cautious, but they will often add an update note to an article that contains a factual error. On Wikipedia, do not edit your own company page directly; propose the change on the article's talk page with reliable published sources, in line with the conflict-of-interest guidelines.

An AI answer is only as accurate as the weakest widely cited page about you. Fix that page, and the answer has nothing left to repeat.

Feedback tools and formal requests to AI providers

Every major assistant has a feedback mechanism, and using it is worthwhile but rarely sufficient on its own. ChatGPT and Gemini let you rate a response and explain what is wrong, AI Overviews have a feedback option on each summary, and Perplexity lets you flag answers.

When an answer contains incorrect personal data about an identifiable person, such as a founder or manager, the GDPR offers stronger tools. Article 16 gives a right to rectification and Article 17 a right to erasure, and OpenAI, Google and other providers have privacy request forms for these cases. The Garante per la protezione dei dati personali has already taken enforcement action against an AI chatbot provider in Italy, which shows that the authority treats these systems as data controllers. A company as such is not protected by the GDPR, but false statements about its executives are, and seriously damaging falsehoods may also raise questions of defamation under Italian law.

ToolBest forRealistic effect
In-product feedbackAny factual errorSignal to the provider; no guaranteed change
GDPR rectification requestWrong data about a named personFormal response required; may lead to filtering of outputs
Source correctionErrors about the companyThe most durable fix for retrieval-based answers

Strengthening reputation in AI answers over time

Lasting accuracy comes from giving models plenty of consistent, recent and authoritative material about your business. A single corrected page can be outweighed by ten older pages repeating the mistake.

Publish clear, factual content that answers the questions customers ask an assistant: what the company does, where it operates in Italy, who leads it, how it handles complaints. Encourage coverage in reputable trade media, keep review profiles active, and make sure the Italian and English versions of your site say the same thing. Companies that already invest in search visibility will find that the same assets protect them in AI answers, a link explained in our guide to protecting your company's reputation before problems arise.

How to monitor AI mentions of your brand

To monitor AI mentions effectively, run a fixed set of prompts across the main assistants every month and record the answers, the cited sources and any errors. Because responses vary between sessions, repeat each prompt more than once and look for patterns rather than single outputs.

  1. Write ten to twenty prompts covering your brand name, products, leadership, reviews and comparisons with alternatives, in Italian and English.
  2. Test them in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Google AI Overviews, logged out where possible.
  3. Save the answers with date and sources in a shared spreadsheet.
  4. Flag new errors, trace them to their sources and add them to the correction table.
  5. Recheck corrected items after each crawl cycle to confirm the change.
